gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Trailcampro measured the $59.99 FLEX-M at 65.7 s picture recovery, so roughly one photo a minute, against 3.6 s for the FLEX DARK, or that Trailcampro's 2026 shootout ranks the FLEX-M #33 of 40 on flash range while the FLEX DARK came #5 and won the cellular flash-range category.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages and the top uncited results. The cited spypoint.com FLEX-M page has no trigger, recovery, battery or range figure for the FLEX-M. Its only test claim is that the FLEX-M 'placed first in trailcampro.com's 2024 Cellular Trail Camera Flash Range Shootout', which Trailcampro's 2026 ranking of #33 contradicts. The cited Spypoint blog (2023-05-11) gives only price and 28 MP / 720p. trailcamspecs.com says it does not test and gives no measurements. camandcanopy.com gives maker claims (FLEX DARK 0.3 s / 100 ft, FLEX-M2 0.4 s) and names Trailcampro's 2026 flash-range winner without a number. Outdoor Life (uncited, 2026-09-25) has the only rival figures: Alex Robinson found the FLEX-M2 did not trigger at 110 ft, some photos took a few hours to transmit, and Duracell AAs lasted about 1.5 months. None of these pages has a recovery time, a battery-runtime comparison across the free-plan models, or the 2026 flash-range ranking.
decides: All three free-plan cameras ChatGPT listed trigger at about the same speed, under 0.4 s in Trailcampro's lab. They differ in recovery and at night. At 65.7 s recovery the FLEX-M misses follow-up shots of the same animal, and it ranks #33 of 40 on flash range. The FLEX DARK ($119.99 at Best Buy per ChatGPT's card) recovers in 3.6 s, ranked #5 of 40 on flash range, sent a photo in 47.6 s in Trailcampro's test and lasted 3.9 months against 3.3 on lithium AAs. So the FLEX-M is still the cheapest way onto the 100-photo free plan, but the FLEX DARK is the better pick for night use or several shots in a row. Trailcampro has published no full lab numbers for the FLEX-M2, so the middle card can't be ranked on these measures.
